phases.title: The face
phases.summary: The head from every angle, and expressions.
phases.intro: The face is what people look at first. You'll build a complete head from every angle, with its eyes, nose, mouth and hair, then give it emotions.

phases.title: The body
phases.intro: Your character gets a body with the right proportions, poses full of life, hands that talk and clothes that fold in the right places.

weeks.title: The head from every angle
weeks.goal: Build a complete manga head, eyes, nose, mouth, ears and hair, from the front, in three-quarter view and in profile.
weeks.summary: Build the head in volume, then learn the eyes, the nose, the mouth and the hair, one a day.
weeks.deliverable: your character's head from the front, in 3/4 view and in profile.

days.title: The head as a volume
days.summary: A manga head isn't a flat circle: it's a ball you carve. Four steps, always the same.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 quick circles of the same size: they'll be your skulls.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Every manga head is built in the same 4 steps, whichever way it turns. Follow them in order.

method.title: The skull: a sphere
method.text: A circle for the skull. It's the main volume: everything else hangs on it.

method.title: The side plane
method.text: Cut a slice off the side of the sphere: that's the temple, where the ear will go.

method.title: The axis of the face
method.text: A curved vertical line through the middle of the face. It follows the turn of the head.

method.title: Jaw and chin
method.text: Come down from each side of the skull to the chin. In manga, the chin is thin and a little pointed.

steps.tip: When the head turns, draw the axis of the face first: it decides where the eyes, nose and mouth go.

steps.title: Follow the steps
steps.instructions: Build 3 heads following the 4 steps: one from the front, one in three-quarter view, one in profile.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here are finished faces, without their construction. Pick 2, find the sphere, side plane, axis and jaw under each one, then draw them.

steps.title: Challenge: a head in 1 minute
steps.instructions: Draw this head in 1 minute, construction included. Do it twice.

days.title: The eyes
days.summary: Build a manga eye step by step, then put it on a face, from the front, in 3/4 and in profile.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: A manga eye is always built in the same order: the shape, the eyelids, the iris, the highlights.

method.title: The shape
method.text: A lying almond, a little pointier on the outer side. It sets the size of the eye.

method.title: The eyelids
method.text: Go over the top of the almond with a thick curved line: the upper eyelid, what makes a manga eye. At the bottom, just a short thin line.

method.title: The iris
method.text: A big standing oval, cut at the top by the eyelid, reaching almost down to the lower lid.

method.title: Pupil and highlights
method.text: A dark pupil in the middle of the iris, 1 or 2 white highlights at the top, and a few lashes at the outer corner.

steps.tip: Put the highlights on the same side in both eyes: the light comes from one place.

steps.title: Follow the steps
steps.instructions: Build 2 eyes following the 4 stages: a left eye and a right eye. The pointed corner always faces the outside of the face.

steps.title: On the face
steps.instructions: A beautiful eye in the wrong place spoils the whole face. Four rules are enough to place it.

method.title: The eye line
method.text: Halfway down the head, between the top of the skull and the chin. Lower, the character looks younger.

method.title: The gap
method.text: The width of one eye between the two eyes.

method.title: In 3/4 view
method.text: The far eye gets narrower and moves closer to the nose; the near one keeps its shape.

method.title: In profile
method.text: You see only one eye, shaped like an arrowhead, and the iris becomes a thin oval.

steps.tip: Draw the eye line all the way across the head: it follows the curve of the ball when the head turns.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here are 3 faces without eyes, from the front, in 3/4 and in profile. Draw their outline, mark the eye line, then build their eyes with the 4 stages.

steps.title: Challenge: 3 types of eyes
steps.instructions: Draw 3 pairs of eyes for 3 characters: big and round for a gentle one, almond-shaped for a calm one, thin and sharp for a rival. Only the almond and the size of the iris change.

days.title: The nose
days.summary: A small wedge on the face: how to build it, and the 3 types of manga nose.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 small triangles the size of a nose, turned every which way: it's the basic shape of the nose.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Even when it's a single stroke, a manga nose is a volume: a small wedge on the face, of which you only draw a part.

method.title: Where it goes
method.text: On the center line of the face, halfway between the eye line and the chin.

method.title: The wedge
method.text: Sketch it lightly: a long triangle for the bridge, and a small flat underside where the nostrils are.

method.title: One side only
method.text: Choose where the light comes from and ink only the shaded side, or only the underside. Erase the rest.

method.title: When the head turns
method.text: In 3/4, the tip sticks out a little past the center line, toward the way the head turns. In profile, the nose comes out of the face outline as a small triangle.

steps.tip: Always sketch the whole wedge lightly, even for a one-stroke nose: it's what puts it in the right place.

steps.title: Types of noses
steps.instructions: The same wedge gives 3 different noses, depending on what you keep. Choose by the character's age and style.

method.title: The dot
method.text: A dot or a tiny line under the tip. For cute characters and children.

method.title: The triangle
method.text: The shaded side and the underside form a small triangle. For teens and adults.

method.title: The drawn nose
method.text: The bridge, the tip and the nostrils. For realistic styles and older characters.

steps.tip: A character keeps the same type of nose from every angle: it helps people recognize them.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here are a child, a teen and an adult, without noses. Draw their faces and give each one the type of nose that suits them, right on the center line.

steps.title: Challenge: 5 profiles
steps.instructions: Draw 5 profiles in one line each, from forehead to chin, changing only the nose: small, upturned, straight, pointed, hooked.

days.title: The mouth
days.summary: Build a manga mouth, closed or open, with its teeth and tongue, from every angle.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 little mouth lines, each with a different curve: straight, arched, wavy, lopsided.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: In manga a mouth fits in 1 to 3 strokes. But those strokes follow the shape of the face.

method.title: Where it goes
method.text: On the center line, closer to the nose than to the chin: a third of the way from one to the other.

method.title: The line
method.text: A slightly curved stroke, narrower than the space between the eyes. Its corners set the mood.

method.title: The lower lip
method.text: A short stroke under the line is enough to suggest the lip. No need to outline the lips.

method.title: When the head turns
method.text: In 3/4, the far side of the mouth gets shorter. In profile, only a small notch remains under the nose, set back a little.

steps.tip: If your mouth has more than 3 strokes, remove some: it will look more manga.

steps.title: Opening the mouth
steps.instructions: An open mouth is the line opening into a shape, with what shows inside.

method.title: Slightly open
method.text: A tiny oval or a small triangle in place of the line.

method.title: Open
method.text: A D shape lying down: flat side at the top for a smile, rounder and taller for a shout.

method.title: The teeth
method.text: A simple white band under the top of the mouth, without drawing each tooth.

method.title: The tongue
method.text: A curve at the bottom of the open mouth: it fills the back and adds depth.

steps.tip: Fill the inside of the mouth in gray or black: the shape reads at once.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here is a character talking. Draw their face twice in 3/4 view saying "Ah" and "Oh": wide open, then round.

steps.title: Challenge: a big bite
steps.instructions: Draw a character biting into a rice ball: the mouth wide open, the upper teeth showing, the cheeks puffed up.

days.title: Hair
days.summary: A mass around the skull, locks starting from the parting, and your character's head finally complete.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 locks of hair in one stroke each: wide at the root, thin at the tip, curved like an S or a C.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Hair isn't hundreds of lines: it's a volume sitting on the skull, cut into a few big locks.

method.title: The hairline
method.text: It runs along the top of the forehead, a little below the top of the skull, and comes down in front of the ear: a C on the side plane, from the top of the eyes to the bottom of the nose.

method.title: The mass
method.text: Hair has thickness: draw its overall shape around the skull, a little bigger than it, never stuck to it.

method.title: The parting and the locks
method.text: Choose where the parting is: every lock starts from there. Cut the mass into big pointed locks.

method.title: Locks follow the ball
method.text: In 3/4 and in profile, the locks wrap around the skull, like the construction lines of the head.

steps.tip: Always sketch the mass lightly before the first lock: otherwise the hair sticks to the skull.

steps.title: Types of hairstyles
steps.instructions: Every hairstyle is built the same way. What changes is the shape of the mass and how the locks are drawn.

method.title: Short and spiky
method.text: A round mass bristling with triangle locks pointing every way.

method.title: Straight
method.text: Long, almost straight locks that fall under their own weight and split into points.

method.title: Wavy or curly
method.text: S-shaped locks, or spirals gathered in clumps, never one by one.

method.title: Tied up
method.text: Ponytail, pigtails, bun: draw the hair tie first, then the hair pulled toward it and the tuft coming out of it.

steps.tip: Whatever the hairstyle, leave 2 or 3 small locks sticking out: they bring it to life.

steps.title: Your character, 3 angles
steps.instructions: Invent your character and draw their complete head from the front, in 3/4 and in profile: construction, eyes, nose, mouth, then their hairstyle. Long horizontal lines keep the eyes, nose and mouth at the same height on all 3.

lessons.title: Building the head in three steps

steps.title: The skull
steps.text: Start with a sphere or an egg shape.

steps.title: The side plane and the axis
steps.text: Cut a flattened face on the side of the skull: that's the temple, where the ear will go. Then draw the vertical axis down the middle of the face: it curves as the head turns.

steps.title: The eye line and the jaw
steps.text: Draw the eye line: it follows the surface of the face and turns with the head. Then connect the sides of the skull to the chin with simple lines.

lessons.callout: Don't jump straight to the eyes, the hair and the final outline. First check that the head is correctly oriented.

lessons.title: Coach's exercise: the rotation
lessons.intro: Imagine a small box inside the skull, as a guide to orient the head. Turn this guide, then place the features of the face on its surface.
lessons.callout: This exercise helps you understand difficult angles instead of memorizing a single recipe for the eyes or the jaw.

weeks.title: Expressions
weeks.goal: Build each emotion with the eyebrows, eyelids and mouth, control how strong it is, then push it the manga way.
weeks.summary: Joy, sadness, anger, surprise and fear, one a day, then the manga codes.
weeks.deliverable: an expression sheet of your character with 6 emotions.

days.title: Joy
days.summary: Build a smile with 3 levers, eyebrows, eyelids and mouth, then its 4 shades.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: An emotion is always built in the same order: eyebrows, eyelids, mouth. Joy is all three going up.

method.title: The eyebrows
method.text: Relaxed and slightly arched, a little raised. Never frowning.

method.title: The eyelids
method.text: The rising cheeks push the lower lid up: the eye squints. In a big smile, it closes into an arc.

method.title: The mouth
method.text: The corners go up. The stronger the joy, the more the mouth opens into a D, flat side on top.

method.title: The cheeks
method.text: A small curve under the eye, or a few blush lines: the cheeks lift with the smile.

steps.tip: Real joy shows in the eyes: if only the mouth smiles, the smile looks forced.

steps.title: The 4 smiles
steps.instructions: Joy has several levels: the same levers, pushed more or less.

method.title: The soft smile
method.text: Closed mouth in a small curve, eyes open and calm.

method.title: The big smile
method.text: Open mouth showing the upper teeth, squinting eyes.

method.title: The laugh
method.text: Eyes closed in arcs, mouth wide open, head thrown back.

method.title: The awkward smile
method.text: Small smile, eyebrows lifted in the middle, eyes looking away.

steps.tip: Pick the smile that fits the personality: a reserved character rarely grins with all their teeth.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here are 3 characters in 3/4 view. Give each one a different smile: soft for the first, big for the second, a laugh for the third.

steps.title: Challenge: no mouth
steps.instructions: Draw a face with the mouth hidden behind a scarf: it must clearly be smiling, just from the eyes and cheeks.

days.title: Sadness
days.summary: Eyebrows lifting in the middle, eyes dropping, and 4 ways to be sad.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Same order, eyebrows, eyelids, mouth, but everything drops, except the middle of the eyebrows.

method.title: The eyebrows
method.text: The inner ends go up, the outer ends go down: a slope like a tent.

method.title: The eyelids
method.text: The upper lid drops over the iris, the gaze lowers. The eyes shine: add one more highlight.

method.title: The mouth
method.text: The corners go down. Closed, it wobbles in a small wave; open, it turns square.

method.title: The head drops
method.text: The eye line curves downward and the top of the skull shows more: the whole head says sadness.

steps.tip: Sadness is held back: very sad eyebrows with a tight mouth make it stronger.

steps.title: The 4 sadnesses
steps.instructions: From a small letdown to sobbing, sadness builds in stages.

method.title: The pout
method.text: Eyebrows barely lifted, lower lip pushed out a little.

method.title: Teary eyes
method.text: A line of water on the lower lid and big trembling highlights.

method.title: Tears
method.text: Drops running from the corner of the eye along the cheek.

method.title: Sobbing
method.text: Eyes squeezed shut, mouth wide open and square, streams of tears.

steps.tip: A tear follows the curve of the cheek: draw it like a drop sliding over a ball.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Draw these 3 sad characters with their head tilted down: the eye line curved, the gaze looking away.

steps.title: Challenge: holding back tears
steps.instructions: Draw a character smiling to hide their sadness: sad eyebrows, teary eyes, but a small smile.

days.title: Anger
days.summary: V-shaped eyebrows, narrowing eyes, and anger from annoyance to fury.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Still eyebrows, eyelids, mouth. Anger pulls everything toward the middle of the face.

method.title: The eyebrows
method.text: The inner ends drop toward the nose: a V. Two small creases form between the brows.

method.title: The eyelids
method.text: The upper lid comes down over the iris and straightens: the gaze hardens. Smaller pupils.

method.title: The mouth
method.text: Closed, it tightens into a straight line or shows clenched teeth; open, it's a shout shaped like a trapezoid.

method.title: Nose and cheeks
method.text: The top of the nose wrinkles and the cheeks tighten: a few lines are enough.

steps.tip: The closer the eyebrows are to the eyes, the more threatening the character looks.

steps.title: The 4 angers
steps.instructions: Anger has its levels, and each one says something about the character.

method.title: Annoyed
method.text: Eyebrows barely frowning, half-closed eyes, mouth twisted to the side.

method.title: Sulking
method.text: V-shaped eyebrows, puffed cheeks, pressed lips, eyes to the side.

method.title: Furious
method.text: Eyebrows very low, clenched teeth, creases on the nose.

method.title: Shouting
method.text: Mouth wide open in a trapezoid, teeth showing, eyes wide.

steps.tip: Pick the level that fits the personality: a calm one stays annoyed where a hothead shouts.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here are 2 characters arguing, face to face in profile. Draw them: one sulking, the other shouting.

steps.title: Challenge: anger, head to toe
steps.instructions: Draw a furious character from head to toe: V-shaped eyebrows, clenched teeth, clenched fists, raised shoulders. The whole body must show the anger, not just the face.

days.title: Surprise and fear
days.summary: Eyes opening wide: what separates a nice surprise from real fear.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Eyebrows, eyelids, mouth: surprise and fear open everything. The difference is in the details.

method.title: The eyebrows
method.text: Surprise: they go up high and stay rounded. Fear: they go up too, but lift in the middle.

method.title: The eyelids
method.text: Wide open, with white all around the iris. In fear, the pupil becomes tiny.

method.title: The mouth
method.text: Surprise: a relaxed open circle. Fear: the mouth stretches sideways and trembles.

method.title: The head
method.text: In fear, the head sinks into the shoulders and pulls back; in surprise, it straightens up.

steps.tip: The more white around the iris, the stronger the emotion.

steps.title: The 4 reactions
steps.instructions: From astonishment to terror, four reactions to know.

method.title: Astonished
method.text: Raised eyebrows, slightly bigger eyes, mouth in a small o.

method.title: Shocked
method.text: Eyes wide open, small pupils, mouth dropping wide open.

method.title: Worried
method.text: Eyebrows lifted in the middle, eyes darting to the side, pressed lips.

method.title: Terrified
method.text: Tiny pupils, stretched trembling mouth, sweat on the forehead.

steps.tip: Add shaky lines around a terrified character: you can feel them shiver.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Copy these 2 faces in 3/4 view: one surprised, one scared. Place the eyebrows first, then the eyelids, then the mouth, and leave plenty of white around the iris.

steps.title: Challenge: surprise in profile
steps.instructions: Draw a surprised character in profile: eyebrows going up, a round eye, an open mouth, the head pulling back.

days.title: Manga codes
days.summary: Sweat drops, veins, blushes, distorted eyes: manga's symbols, then your character's expression sheet.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: These symbols are a language every manga reader knows. They add to the expression, they don't replace it.

method.title: The sweat drop
method.text: A big drop on the temple or behind the head: awkwardness, unease.

method.title: The anger vein
method.text: A cross with curved branches on the forehead or temple: annoyance building up.

method.title: The blush
method.text: Small slanted lines across the cheeks and nose: embarrassment, love, fever.

method.title: Distorted eyes
method.text: Spirals for dizziness, hearts for love, stars for wonder.

steps.tip: One or two codes per face is plenty: beyond that, the emotion stops reading.

steps.title: Comic reactions
steps.instructions: In funny scenes, manga goes further: the face gets simpler and stretches.

method.title: Blank eyes
method.text: Two empty ovals, no iris: the character is in shock.

method.title: Waterfall tears
method.text: Two streams gushing from closed eyes: grief blown up for laughs.

method.title: The dropping jaw
method.text: The mouth opens down to the chest: surprise pushed to the absurd.

method.title: The simplified face
method.text: No nose, dot or line eyes, a triangle mouth: the character almost turns chibi.

steps.tip: A comic reaction works best right after a serious expression.

steps.title: Your expression sheet
steps.instructions: Draw 6 emotions of your character on one page, in 2 rows of 3: joy, sadness, anger, surprise, fear and a comic reaction. Same head and hairstyle on all of them, at most one manga code per face.

weeks.title: The body and its proportions
weeks.goal: Build a manga body with the right proportions, head to toe: torso, arms, legs, then the whole character.
weeks.summary: Proportions, the torso, the arms, the legs, then your character full body.
weeks.deliverable: your character full body, from the front and in profile.

days.title: Proportions
days.summary: Measure a character with their own head, and the proportions by age and style.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: To stop getting leg lengths wrong, measure your character with their own head, in 4 stages.

method.title: The line and the head
method.text: Draw the character's height, then cut it into head heights, from the top of the skull to the chin.

method.title: The landmarks
method.text: 2 heads: the chest. 3: the navel. 3.5: the crotch, the middle of the body. 5: the knees. 7: the feet.

method.title: The widths
method.text: Shoulders about 2 heads wide, hips about 1.5 heads.

method.title: The arms
method.text: With the arms down, the elbow falls at the waist and the fingertips at mid-thigh.

steps.tip: The classic trap: legs too short. If your character looks squashed, lengthen the legs, not the torso.

steps.title: Ages and styles
steps.instructions: The number of heads changes with the character's age and the manga's style.

method.title: Chibi
method.text: 2 to 3 heads: a huge head, a small round body.

method.title: The child
method.text: 4 to 5 heads: big head, short legs, no defined waist.

method.title: The teen
method.text: 6 to 7 heads: the most common in manga.

method.title: The adult and the hero
method.text: 7.5 to 8 heads, up to 9 for an action hero: small head, long legs.

steps.tip: Keep the same head size to compare: only the body grows from one age to the next.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Pick one of these characters, mark their landmarks next to them (head, chest, navel, crotch, knees) and redraw them following those marks.

days.title: The torso
days.summary: An egg rib cage, a box pelvis and the belly linking them: the center of the whole body.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 eggs point down and 10 flat little boxes, from every angle.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Before muscles and clothes, the torso is built with two volumes, in 4 stages.

method.title: Neck and shoulders
method.text: A cylinder for the neck, then the shoulder line, a little below the chin.

method.title: The rib cage
method.text: An egg, point down, from the shoulders to the bottom of the ribs, a little above the navel.

method.title: The pelvis
method.text: A slightly flattened box, from the navel to the crotch.

method.title: Belly and spine
method.text: Between rib cage and pelvis, a gap: the belly, which bends and twists. A curved line, the spine, links everything at the back.

steps.tip: Never stick the rib cage to the pelvis: without the belly's gap, your character can't bend.

steps.title: The 4 torsos
steps.instructions: With the same two volumes, you change the character's silhouette.

method.title: Boy
method.text: Wide rib cage and square shoulders, narrow pelvis: a V.

method.title: Girl
method.text: Smaller rib cage, slim waist, pelvis as wide as the shoulders: an hourglass.

method.title: Slim
method.text: Narrow, elongated volumes, a thin neck.

method.title: Heavy-set
method.text: A huge rib cage, a thick neck, shoulders rising almost to the ears.

steps.tip: Exaggerate the differences first, then soften: playing it too safe makes every body look the same.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here are dressed characters. For 2 of them, find the torso under the clothes: draw their rib cage and pelvis, then the outline.

steps.title: Challenge: side view
steps.instructions: Draw a torso in side view: the rib cage leans a little forward, the pelvis backward, and the back makes an S.

days.title: The arms
days.summary: Two cylinders, three joints, and the positions of a bending arm.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 quick cylinders, standing, lying down and tilted: two ellipses and two lines.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: An arm is built in 4 stages, from the shoulder to the hand, without worrying about muscles at first.

method.title: The shoulder
method.text: A ball at the end of the shoulder line: the whole arm turns around it.

method.title: Two cylinders
method.text: Upper arm and forearm have the same length; the upper one is thicker.

method.title: Elbow and wrist
method.text: A small ball at the elbow, at waist level, a smaller one at the wrist. The hand stays a mitten for now.

method.title: The outline
method.text: A round bump for the shoulder, then soft curves: never two parallel lines.

steps.tip: When the arm bends, the upper cylinder passes in front of or behind the lower one, never end to end.

steps.title: The 4 positions
steps.instructions: The same cylinders, bent differently: four positions to know.

method.title: Down by the side
method.text: Both cylinders aligned, the hand at mid-thigh.

method.title: Bent
method.text: The elbow stays near the waist, the forearm rises: the cylinders overlap at the elbow.

method.title: Raised
method.text: The shoulder rises with the arm: the shoulder ball lifts toward the ear.

method.title: Crossed
method.text: The forearms pass in front of the torso: the front one hides part of the other.

steps.tip: An arm raised straight up is longer than you think: the elbow reaches about the top of the head.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here are arms in varied positions. Redraw 3 of them: shoulder, cylinders and joints first, then the outline.

steps.title: Challenge: arms crossed
steps.instructions: Draw a character standing with arms crossed over the chest, from the front: which arm goes in front, which behind?

days.title: Legs and feet
days.summary: Thigh, knee, calf, then foot: legs that really carry the character.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 simple feet as long triangles, in profile then from the front.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: A leg is built in 4 stages, from the hip down to the foot.

method.title: The hip
method.text: A ball on each side of the pelvis: the legs start there, not from the bottom of the pelvis.

method.title: Thigh and knee
method.text: The thigh is the biggest cylinder in the body. The knee falls halfway between hip and foot.

method.title: The calf
method.text: It bulges at the back of the leg, then thins down to the ankle.

method.title: The foot
method.text: A long triangle, almost as long as the head. The ankle bone sits higher on the inside than on the outside.

steps.tip: A leg is never a tube: a curve on one side answers a straighter line on the other.

steps.title: The 4 positions
steps.instructions: Standing, walking, sitting, kneeling: the legs change everything.

method.title: Standing
method.text: The legs angle slightly inward: the feet come together under the body.

method.title: Walking
method.text: One leg in front, one behind: the back knee bends and the heel lifts.

method.title: Sitting
method.text: The thighs go horizontal and the knees come up to hip level.

method.title: Kneeling
method.text: The knee touches the ground, the back foot bends on its toes.

steps.tip: Always draw the ground: a short line under the feet is enough to make the character stand.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Draw a mannequin in 3 everyday situations: walking, sitting on a step, kneeling to pick something up. Take care of the hip, the knee and the ankle.

steps.title: Challenge: on a chair
steps.instructions: Draw a character sitting on a chair in profile: back, thighs and shins make three lines at almost right angles.

days.title: Your character, full body
days.summary: The whole body put together, front and side view, with your character's silhouette.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 3 standing stick figures in 10 seconds each, landmarks included.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: To put a whole body together, always follow this order, from measuring to outline.

method.title: The lines
method.text: Draw the landmarks across the whole page: top of the head, chin, chest, navel, crotch, knees, feet.

method.title: The stick figure
method.text: A spine, the shoulder line, the hip line, then the limbs down to the landmarks.

method.title: The volumes
method.text: Rib cage, pelvis, arm and leg cylinders, placed on the stick figure.

method.title: Outline and clothes
method.text: An outline in soft curves, then a T-shirt and pants following the volumes.

steps.tip: Draw the whole front view first, then extend each landmark to the side to build the side view.

steps.title: The 4 silhouettes
steps.instructions: Before drawing your character, choose their silhouette: it says who they are before their face does.

method.title: The triangle
method.text: Wide shoulders, narrow hips: a strong character, a hero.

method.title: The hourglass
method.text: Shoulders and hips of the same width, slim waist: elegant, graceful.

method.title: The rectangle
method.text: Everything the same width: a simple, sporty or still childlike character.

method.title: The round
method.text: The belly wider than everything else: a gentle, funny or greedy character.

steps.tip: Fill the silhouette in black: if your character is recognizable from the shape alone, you've won.

steps.title: Your character, full body
steps.instructions: Draw your character full body, front and side view side by side: the lines, the stick figure, the volumes with their silhouette, then the outline and simple clothes.

lessons.title: How to connect the volumes
bullets: The rib cage and the pelvis aren't two rigid rectangles: they are simplified volumes whose shapes you can vary.
The spine connects them and follows a curve.
The abdomen adapts to the distance, the tilt and the twist between the two volumes.
The shoulder line and the hip line are orientation guides. They aren't always parallel.
Draw the volumes as if they were transparent at first, then clean up the outlines once their orientation is right.
lessons.callout: The test: if you can tell which way the chest faces and which way the pelvis faces without adding a single muscle or piece of clothing, your construction is starting to work.

lessons.title: Exercises for each part

steps.title: Arms
steps.text: Draw an upper arm and a forearm in ten orientations, then bend the elbow at different angles. Careful: the elbow, the wrist and the shoulder aren't interchangeable and don't connect the same way.

steps.title: Legs
steps.text: Build the thigh, the lower leg and the foot. Practice with sitting, standing, crouching and moving poses.

steps.title: Hands
steps.text: Start with a box for the palm. Add the fingers as simplified segments, respecting their length and direction. Work on open hands first, then fists, and finally more complex gestures.

steps.title: Feet
steps.text: Build a wedge-shaped volume before adding the toes. Check the heel, the sole and the orientation of the ankle.

lessons.callout: Don't look for muscles and tendons yet. First learn to place the volumes and the joints correctly.

weeks.title: Poses
weeks.goal: Get your character moving: a line of action, weight that sits right, a twist, depth, and poses that tell something.
weeks.summary: Line of action, balance, twist, foreshortening, then action poses.
weeks.deliverable: 3 poses of your character that tell a story.

days.title: The line of action
days.summary: One curve through the whole body, and 4 lines for 4 energies.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 curves in one stroke each, top to bottom: Cs and Ss, more and more curved.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: A well-built mannequin can still look stiff. To make it move, start with a line, even before the head.

method.title: The curve
method.text: A single line from the head to the foot carrying the weight.

method.title: The stick figure
method.text: The spine follows the line; the shoulders and hips cross it.

method.title: The mannequin
method.text: Rib cage and pelvis sit on the curve, the limbs carry it to the end.

method.title: The outline
method.text: Go over the pose without breaking the curve: the back and the supporting leg follow it.

steps.tip: Even a calm standing character leans a little: avoid the perfectly straight line.

steps.title: The 4 lines
steps.instructions: The shape of the line sets the energy of the pose.

method.title: The C
method.text: One curve: the character pushes, pulls or leans.

method.title: The S
method.text: Two curves: a walk, an elegant pose, a relaxed body.

method.title: The I
method.text: Almost straight: a calm character, or one stretched with their whole body, as in a jump straight up.

method.title: The big arc
method.text: A very arched C: action, a strike, momentum.

steps.tip: The more curved the line, the more energy the pose has.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Pick 3 poses from the sheet. For each one, draw its line of action first, then build its mannequin on it.

steps.title: Challenge: 30 seconds
steps.instructions: Draw 4 poses in 30 seconds each, from photos or people around you: only the line of action.

days.title: Foreshortening
days.summary: The arm coming at you, the leg going away: drawing depth.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 6 cylinders seen more and more from the end: the last one is just a circle.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: A limb coming toward you is built in 4 stages, with cylinders.

method.title: The direction
method.text: Draw the limb's axis: it's very short, since it points at you.

method.title: The ellipses
method.text: The ends of the cylinders become almost circles: rounder as they face you.

method.title: Near is big
method.text: A hand reaching at you can be as big as the head: enlarge what's in front.

method.title: The overlap
method.text: The front cylinder hides the start of the one behind: draw it first.

steps.tip: Reach toward a mirror or take a photo: you'll see your forearm disappear behind your hand.

steps.title: The 4 foreshortenings
steps.instructions: Four situations where depth changes everything.

method.title: Arm reaching at you
method.text: A huge hand, the arm almost hidden behind it.

method.title: Leg coming forward
method.text: A kick at you: the sole gets bigger than the torso.

method.title: Seen from above
method.text: Big head and shoulders, tiny feet at the bottom.

method.title: Seen from below
method.text: Huge feet and legs, a tiny head at the top.

steps.tip: Don't be afraid to exaggerate: a timid foreshortening just looks wrong, a pushed one looks powerful.

steps.title: Challenge: the punch
steps.instructions: Draw a character throwing a punch straight at you: the fist bigger than their head.

days.title: Action poses
days.summary: Running, jumping, striking: the right moment pushed all the way, then your character in 3 poses that tell a story.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 6 lines of action in 5 seconds each: a run, a jump, a punch, a fall...

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: An action pose is built in 4 stages and pushes everything to the max.

method.title: The key moment
method.text: Not the middle of the move: the instant just before (arm pulled back) or just after (the punch flying).

method.title: The pushed line
method.text: Push the line of action further than is possible: manga loves it.

method.title: The diagonal
method.text: Lean the whole pose on a diagonal: it looks in motion, where a vertical pose looks still.

method.title: The silhouette
method.text: Fill your pose in black: the action must still read. Keep the arms and legs away from the body.

steps.tip: Hair and clothes carry the movement on: they fly the opposite way to the character.

steps.title: The 4 actions
steps.instructions: Four actions found in every manga.

method.title: Running
method.text: Body leaning forward, one arm and the opposite leg in front, one foot in the air.

method.title: Jumping
method.text: The body stretched like a bow, legs tucked or stretched behind.

method.title: The punch
method.text: The striking arm and its shoulder go forward, the other arm pulls back for balance.

method.title: The kick
method.text: The supporting leg bends, the chest leans away from the kicking leg.

steps.tip: In every action, something goes back to balance what goes forward.

steps.title: Your character in 3 poses
steps.instructions: Draw your character in 3 poses telling a little story: before (getting ready), during (jumping or striking), after (landing or getting up). Draw the 3 lines of action side by side first, then the mannequins, the outline and the face.

lessons.title: Four tools to bring your poses to life

steps.title: The line of action
steps.text: Before any detail, draw a curve that expresses the overall movement. It keeps poses from being too straight and symmetrical.

steps.title: Opposing axes
steps.text: Tilt the shoulders and the pelvis differently to create a natural movement. They shouldn't both be horizontal all the time.

steps.title: Foreshortening
steps.text: An arm pointing at the viewer looks shorter because it goes into depth. Build it with the axis and the volumes rather than trusting its apparent length.

steps.title: Balance
steps.text: Watch where the weight of the body sits and where it touches the ground. A pose must look like it can hold, or clearly show why the character is falling or jumping.

lessons.title: Essential exercise: turn the torso and the pelvis independently

steps.title: Neutral pose
steps.text: Stack the torso and the pelvis without any real twist. Check their relative sizes and the general axis of the body.

steps.title: Twist
steps.text: Turn the rib cage one way and the pelvis the other. The body must keep a coherent link between the two volumes.

steps.title: Tilt
steps.text: Lean both volumes, then adapt the spine and the shoulders. Watch how the center of gravity moves.

weeks.title: Hands and clothes
weeks.goal: Finish your character: hands that make gestures, clothes that fold and hang in the right places, an outfit that tells who they are.
weeks.summary: The hand, gestures, folds, hanging fabric, then your character's outfit.
weeks.deliverable: your complete character, dressed, in their signature pose.

days.title: The hand in blocks
days.summary: A box palm, cylinder fingers: the most dreaded part becomes simple.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Put your hand on the table and draw its overall shape in 30 seconds, without a single detail.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: A hand is only a box and cylinders. It's built in 4 stages.

method.title: The palm
method.text: A flat box, a little longer than it is wide. The whole hand nearly covers the face.

method.title: The fingers
method.text: Three small cylinders each, shorter and shorter. The knuckles form an arc, and the middle finger is the longest.

method.title: The thumb
method.text: It starts at the bottom of the palm, on the side, with a big pad at its base. It folds toward the palm, not like the fingers.

method.title: The outline
method.text: Round off the cylinders, add a crease at each joint and simple nails. No more.

steps.tip: Your other hand is the perfect model: it's always there and holds any pose you like.

steps.title: The 4 views
steps.instructions: The same hand changes completely depending on where you look from.

method.title: The palm
method.text: Palm creases, the thumb pad, fingers narrowing at the tips.

method.title: The back
method.text: Knuckles in an arc, nails, flatter fingers.

method.title: From the side
method.text: The palm becomes a thin box, the fingers hide behind one another.

method.title: Fingertips first
method.text: The fingers point at you: very short little cylinders, almost circles.

steps.tip: Keep the palm a box from every view: it gives the hand its direction.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here are 3 everyday hands: resting flat on a table, leaning on a knee, hanging by the side. Redraw them: the palm box first, then the fingers.

steps.title: Challenge: your own hand
steps.instructions: Draw your own hand with the fingers spread wide, then with the fingers together. 1 minute each, in blocks.

days.title: Folds
days.summary: Clothes fold where the body bends or pulls: find those points and the folds come by themselves.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 3 cylinders and wrap them in spiral folds, like a rolled-up sleeve.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: A fold is never random. It's drawn in 4 stages, starting from the body.

method.title: The body underneath
method.text: Draw the arm, the leg or the torso in volumes: the fabric will rest on it.

method.title: Pull points
method.text: Find where the fabric pulls: shoulder, elbow, knee, waist. Mark them with a small circle.

method.title: The fabric outline
method.text: The garment follows the body without sticking to it, tighter near the pull points.

method.title: The folds
method.text: Draw the folds from the pull points, in strokes that taper at the end.

steps.tip: Three well-placed folds beat fifteen random ones.

steps.title: The 4 folds
steps.instructions: Depending on how the fabric is held, it makes 4 kinds of folds.

method.title: The star
method.text: Lines radiating from a pull point: the armpit, the crotch.

method.title: The zigzag
method.text: In the crook of a bent elbow or knee, the fabric piles up in a zigzag.

method.title: The spiral
method.text: Around a turning arm or leg, the folds wrap around.

method.title: The diamond
method.text: Between two pulling points, the fabric hollows into diamonds: a bending back, an outstretched arm.

steps.tip: Thin fabric makes many small folds, thick fabric a few big ones.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Redraw these 3 folding garments. For each one, find the pull point first, then the type of fold.

steps.title: Challenge: arms up
steps.instructions: Draw a character stretching with both arms up: the T-shirt rides up and the folds start from the armpits.

days.title: Hanging fabric
days.summary: Skirts, capes, wide sleeves, scarves: fabric that hangs and flies in the wind.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 quick waves at the bottom of a bell shape: it's the hem of a skirt.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Hanging fabric is built in 4 stages, from where it hangs down to its edge.

method.title: The hanging point
method.text: The waist for a skirt, the shoulders for a cape: everything hangs from there.

method.title: The overall shape
method.text: A bell or a rectangle hanging down, wider at the bottom than at the top.

method.title: The tubes
method.text: The fabric falls in vertical tubes starting from the hanging point.

method.title: The hem
method.text: The edge makes a wave: each tube bulges forward there, then tucks back.

steps.tip: The hem is a wavy ellipse: see it like the rim of a glass seen from the side.

steps.title: The 4 fabrics
steps.instructions: The same principle for four garments that move.

method.title: The skirt
method.text: Pleated: regular tubes; full: big waves.

method.title: The cape
method.text: It falls from the shoulders down the back and hides part of the body.

method.title: The wide sleeve
method.text: It hangs under the raised arm, like a small curtain.

method.title: The wind
method.text: In the wind, fabric flies away from the movement and unrolls in wider and wider waves.

steps.tip: Hair and fabric follow the same wind: make them fly the same way.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Draw 2 seated characters: one in a long skirt, the other in a long coat. The fabric falls from the knees to the floor in tubes.

steps.title: Challenge: in the wind
steps.instructions: Draw a character standing in the wind: their cape, their scarf and their hair all fly the same way.

days.title: Your character's outfit
days.summary: An outfit that tells who they are, then your complete character, in their signature pose.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 5 collars around a cylinder neck: crew neck, shirt, hood, sailor collar, turtleneck.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: An outfit is drawn in layers, over the body, in 4 stages.

method.title: Body first
method.text: Draw the whole mannequin, even under a long coat: it's what carries the outfit.

method.title: Thickness
method.text: Fabric rests on the body without sticking to it: leave a small gap, bigger for thick fabric.

method.title: The edges
method.text: Collars, hems, belts and cuffs wrap around the body: draw them as curves, never as straight lines.

method.title: A detail that tells
method.text: One or two details say who they are: a badge, a scarf, gloves, a cape.

steps.tip: Mix a thick fabric and a thin one (jacket and T-shirt, cape and shirt): the contrast makes the outfit easier to read.

steps.title: The 4 outfits
steps.instructions: Four basic manga outfits, each with its own rules.

method.title: School uniform
method.text: Blazer or sailor collar, pleated skirt or straight trousers: clean, symmetrical lines.

method.title: Sportswear
method.text: Soft, close-fitting fabrics, lots of small folds at the joints.

method.title: Everyday clothes
method.text: Hoodie, jeans, sneakers: thick fabrics, wide folds, layers.

method.title: Adventure gear
method.text: Coat, cape, belts, boots: layers and accessories that tell of the journey.

steps.tip: Choose the outfit from your character's life: where do they go, what do they do all day?

steps.title: Your complete character
steps.instructions: Draw your character full body, dressed, in their signature pose: line of action, mannequin, outfit and folds, a hand gesture, and their expression.

practice.title: Build a character
practice.goal: Volumes, perspective and the mannequin: the base of every body drawing. Do these sessions whenever you like, in any order.

days.title: Your character in volumes
days.summary: The core method: a sphere, two boxes and cylinders. Learn it on a model, then do it on your own on a new character.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Fill a corner of the page with quick lines and ovals, moving from the shoulder. Just to loosen up your hand.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Every manga character is built from the same simple shapes. Spot them on the model, in this order.

method.title: The head: a sphere
method.text: The skull is a circle, with the chin coming down to a soft point under it. The head then becomes the unit you measure the whole body with.

method.title: The chest: a box on top
method.text: A rectangle with rounded corners, from the shoulders down to the bottom of the ribs. It's the biggest shape of the body: place it first, under the head.

method.title: The pelvis: a box below
method.text: A smaller rectangle under the chest, with a gap between the two: that's the belly, the part that bends and twists.

method.title: Arms and legs: cylinders
method.text: Two cylinders per limb, joined by a small ball at the shoulder, elbow, hip and knee. The tubes get thinner towards the hands and feet.

steps.tip: Draw all these shapes with very light strokes: they're scaffolding you'll erase at the end.

steps.title: Copy the construction
steps.instructions: Copy only the model's construction: the head, the two boxes, then the cylinders. No details, no clothes.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.instructions: Here's a new character, with no help this time. Find its shapes yourself: the head, the chest box, the pelvis box, then the cylinders of the arms and legs.

steps.title: 1-minute challenge
steps.instructions: Redraw the same character in volumes, but in 1 minute. Going fast forces you to keep only what matters.

days.title: The box in perspective
days.summary: The box is the volume that shows where your character is facing. Learn to turn it.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 10 quick squares, then 10 diamonds.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: A box holds in 3 directions. Set them right and it turns any way you like.

method.title: One face
method.text: Start with one face in perspective: a slightly distorted square.

method.title: The depth
method.text: Three parallel edges leave its corners, all in the same direction.

method.title: Close the box
method.text: Join the ends of the edges, and draw the hidden edges lightly.

steps.tip: Check your boxes by extending the edges: the ones going the same way should slowly come together.

steps.title: The turning chest
steps.instructions: Draw the chest box 5 times: from the front, three-quarter left and right, in profile and from above. Put the head on top.

steps.title: Challenge: the stack
steps.instructions: Stack 4 boxes of different sizes, each one turned a different way.

days.title: The jointed mannequin
days.summary: Volumes joined by joints: the mannequin that can take any pose.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: The mannequin takes the character's volumes and adds joints to them.

method.title: Chest and pelvis
method.text: The rib cage as an egg, the pelvis as a box, the belly joining them.

method.title: The joints
method.text: Spheres at the shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees and ankles.

method.title: The limbs
method.text: Cylinders between the joints, thinner towards the hands and feet.

steps.tip: When a pose doesn't work, look at the chest and the pelvis first: they're almost always the ones facing the wrong way.

steps.title: Ten mannequins
steps.instructions: Draw 10 small mannequins in 10 poses: walking, sitting, leaning, kneeling, reaching...

steps.title: Challenge: from a photo
steps.instructions: Find a photo of someone moving and rebuild their pose as a mannequin.

days.title: Measuring in heads
days.summary: The rule that makes your characters look right: the body is measured in head heights, from chibi to hero.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: Draw 6 simple heads: a circle, then the chin. Try to keep them the same size: that's your unit of measure.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: In manga, a character's height is counted in stacked heads. Changing that number changes the whole style.

method.title: Teenager: 6 to 7 heads
method.text: The typical shonen hero. The crotch falls around the middle of the body, the knees around the 5th head.

method.title: Adult: 8 heads
method.text: Taller and broader: the shoulders are about 2 heads wide. Action heroes sometimes go up to 9.

method.title: Chibi: 2 to 3 heads
method.text: A huge head, a small box body, short round limbs. Hands and feet become simple rounded shapes.

steps.tip: Two landmarks that always work: the elbow falls at the waist, the fingertips at mid-thigh.

steps.title: One character, three sizes
steps.instructions: Draw the same character three times side by side: as a chibi (3 heads), a teen (7 heads) and an adult (8 heads). First mark the head measures on the side, then build with your volumes.

steps.title: Investigation
steps.instructions: Take a picture from your favorite manga and count how many heads tall the hero is. Write the number next to your drawing: every mangaka has their own rule.

days.title: Shapes tell the character
days.summary: Circle, square, triangle: each shape gives a personality. Create three characters that are complete opposites.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.instructions: 5 circles, 5 squares, 5 triangles, fast and without a ruler.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: Readers see shapes before details. Pick your character's main shape to match their personality.

method.title: Circle: gentle and friendly
method.text: Round face, full cheeks, sloping shoulders. For the cute character, the best friend, the mascot.

method.title: Square: solid and reliable
method.text: Square jaw, big box chest, wide hands. For the strongman, the protector, the mentor.

method.title: Triangle: sharp or threatening
method.text: Pointy chin, V-shaped shoulders, spiky hair. For the rival, the hot-headed hero, the villain.

steps.tip: The silhouette test: fill your character in black. If you can still guess their personality, you picked the right shape.

steps.title: Three characters, three shapes
steps.instructions: Draw three characters in the same standing pose: one all circles, one all squares, one all triangles. Keep the day 1 method (head, boxes, cylinders), then bend each volume towards its shape.

steps.title: Challenge: the mix
steps.instructions: Invent a 4th character mixing two shapes, like a square body with a round face: the tough guy with a big heart.

days.title: From sketch to clean drawing
days.summary: Wrap your volumes in a clean outline, then draw your first character of the week from start to finish.

steps.title: The method
steps.instructions: The volumes are only scaffolding. Here's how to get to the final drawing without losing the construction.

method.title: Build lightly
method.text: Line of action, head, boxes, cylinders: all in very light, almost invisible strokes.

method.title: Wrap the shapes
method.text: Draw the outline on top, rounding it off: it wraps the volumes without copying them. Add the neck, the waist, the calves.

method.title: Details, then clean up
method.text: Hair, face, clothes. Erase the construction, then go over the final lines with a firmer stroke.

steps.tip: Make the outer outline thicker than the inner lines: the character instantly stands out from the page.

steps.title: Your character of the week
steps.instructions: Invent your own character and draw it in full: pick its shape (circle, square or triangle), its height in heads and a pose with a real line of action. Build, wrap, clean up.

steps.title: Look back
steps.instructions: Put your drawing next to your first practice session. Volumes, proportions, shapes: look how far you've come.

lessons.title: How to draw a box correctly

steps.title: Start with one face
steps.text: Draw a square or a rectangle to define the front of your box. It doesn't need to be perfect.

steps.title: Add depth
steps.text: Draw edges coming out of the corners in a consistent direction. Their orientation shows how the box turns in space.

steps.title: Close the volume
steps.text: Add the remaining faces. You can draw the hidden edges with light strokes to understand the whole structure.

lessons.callout: Mistakes to avoid: edges that change direction for no reason, faces that don't meet, or boxes that look like flat shapes. Don't just draw the visible outline: imagine the full volume.

lessons.title: The big exercise: rotating boxes
lessons.intro: Draw 10 to 20 boxes per session, with a different orientation each time.
lessons.callout: Don't chase a perfect perspective with complicated vanishing points right away. Start by understanding how the faces change when the volume turns.

lessons.title: The method you'll use for all anatomy

steps.title: The rib cage
steps.text: Imagine an oval volume or a box with rounded corners. Its axis shows which way the chest faces. You can simplify it to suit the manga style you're aiming for.

steps.title: The pelvis
steps.text: Use a box that can tilt. Its front face shows the orientation of the pelvis. The hips and the legs must connect to this volume.

steps.title: Limbs and joints
steps.text: Use cylinders or tapered shapes for the segments of the limbs, and simple spheres for the shoulders, elbows, wrists, knees and ankles.

lessons.callout: The key principle: a character is a construction in volume before being a drawing of muscles, clothes or outlines.

lessons.title: The cylinder method
lessons.intro: A limb is built with volumes between the joints, not with two random parallel lines.

steps.title: Draw the axis
steps.text: Start with a line that shows the direction of the arm or the leg.

steps.title: Add the volume
steps.text: Place an ellipse at each end, then connect them. Vary the thickness according to the segment of the body.

steps.title: Connect the joints
steps.text: Use simple shapes for the shoulders, elbows and knees. Check the orientation of each segment before drawing the final outline.

topics.title: Drawing basics
topics.summary: Lines, circles, shapes and cubes: every artist's warm-up.
topics.intro: These exercises aren't flashy, but they make your hand steady. Do a few minutes before you draw: your lines will be cleaner and your shapes more accurate.

chapters.title: Confident lines

steps.title: Move from the shoulder
steps.text: For long lines, lock your wrist and move your whole arm. The line gets straighter and more even.

steps.title: Ghost the stroke
steps.text: Place two points, move back and forth above the paper without touching it, then draw in one go.

steps.title: Light first
steps.text: Start with light strokes, then strengthen only the useful lines.

chapters.callout: A quick, slightly curved line beats a slow, shaky one.

chapters.title: Circles and ellipses

steps.title: Go around in one gesture
steps.text: Go around the shape in one fluid motion, two or three times on top, rather than in small hesitant strokes.

steps.title: An ellipse is a tilted circle
steps.text: The more you see the circle from the side, the flatter the ellipse. Its two halves always stay symmetrical.

steps.title: Draw its axis
steps.text: A line through the middle of the ellipse, along its length, helps you keep it straight and even.

chapters.callout: No points at the ends of an ellipse: they stay rounded.

chapters.title: Simple shapes

steps.title: Corners first
steps.text: Place the four corners of a square as light dots, then join them. Easier than drawing side by side.

steps.title: Vary the sizes
steps.text: Switch between small and big shapes: big ones train your arm, small ones your accuracy.

steps.title: Check upside down
steps.text: Turn your page around: tilted sides and wrong angles jump out.

chapters.callout: Draw big enough: a stamp-sized shape teaches you nothing.

chapters.title: From square to cube

steps.title: One face, then depth
steps.text: Draw the front face, then three parallel edges leaving its corners in the same direction.

steps.title: Close the volume
steps.text: Join the ends of the edges: the back face appears. Draw the hidden edges lightly too.

steps.title: Tilt it
steps.text: Do it again with a tilted cube: no edge is horizontal anymore, but parallel edges stay parallel.

chapters.callout: Light hidden edges help you see whether the cube holds together.

tips: Before each session, 1 minute of lines and ellipses is enough to loosen your hand.
Hold your pencil further from the tip for big strokes, closer for details.
Don't erase every mistake right away: spot what doesn't work and correct it on top.
Rotate your page so you always draw in the direction that's most comfortable for your hand.
Work fast rather than perfect: speed makes lines straighter.
topics.practice: A small still life: a cube, a sphere and a cylinder on a table. Build them lightly, hidden edges included, then go over the outlines.

topics.title: Manga eyes
topics.summary: Place them, build them, bring the gaze to life.
topics.intro: The eyes are the first place the reader looks. In manga, they carry the character's style and almost all of their emotion. Well placed and well built, they bring a face to life with very few lines.

chapters.title: Placing the eyes

steps.title: The eye line
steps.text: On the built head, the eyes sit on the horizontal line halfway between the top of the skull and the chin. Manga often lowers them a little for a younger face.

steps.title: One eye apart
steps.text: Leave about the width of one eye between the two. More space looks soft and childlike, less space looks harsh or grown-up.

steps.title: Follow the curve of the head
steps.text: The eyes sit on a sphere: on a three-quarter head, the far eye gets narrower and closer to the edge of the face. Both eyes stay on the eye line, even when it tilts.

steps.title: The eyebrow above
steps.text: Place the eyebrow about half an eye above. It follows the brow ridge and already sets a good part of the expression.

chapters.callout: Flip your drawing horizontally to check it: an eye higher than the other jumps out once mirrored.

chapters.title: Building an eye in four steps

steps.title: The upper eyelid
steps.text: Start with the thickest line: the upper eyelid, like a roof. It decides the shape of the eye, round, almond or stretched.

steps.title: The iris
steps.text: Draw a tall oval, cut at the top by the eyelid. A fully visible iris makes the gaze look shocked or staring: let it touch the upper line.

steps.title: Pupil and highlights
steps.text: Add the pupil in the middle, then one or two highlights on the same side in both eyes, as if a single lamp lit the face. They are what makes the eye shine.

steps.title: The lower eyelid
steps.text: A thinner, shorter line, often broken. The less of it there is, the lighter the drawing looks.

chapters.callout: The highlights must be in the same place in both eyes. If they are not, the character looks cross-eyed.

chapters.title: What changes a gaze
bullets: A high, round eyelid: a gentle or naive character. A low, flat eyelid: a calm, confident or tired one.
The size of the iris: large, the character looks young and open; small, tense, scared or threatening.
Where the irises point: both look at the same spot. Move them together, never one without the other.
Lashes: a few thick strokes at the outer corner are enough. The heavier they are, the more feminine or dramatic the gaze.
The eyebrow: low and close to the nose, it shows anger; raised in the middle, sadness or worry.

chapters.title: One eye in every style
chapters.intro: The same character changes completely with the style of the eyes. Knowing how to switch from one to the other means choosing who your drawing speaks to.

steps.title: Shojo
steps.text: Very big eyes, taller than wide, a huge iris with several highlights and strong lashes. The gaze is soft, dreamy, very expressive.

steps.title: Shonen
steps.text: Eyes wider than tall, a thick upper eyelid slanting slightly toward the nose, a single sharp highlight. The gaze is determined.

steps.title: Seinen
steps.text: Smaller, more realistic eyes, a thinner eyelid with a visible crease, a smaller iris. The gaze is grown-up and serious.

steps.title: Chibi and comedy
steps.text: A black oval with one highlight, or even a single line. The simpler the style, the clearer the expression has to be.

chapters.callout: Keep the same eye style for every character on a page, or they will look like they come from different manga.

tips: Draw both eyes at the same time, going back and forth: you'll see right away if they are the same size.
Start with the upper eyelid, never with the iris: the eyelid gives the shape.
White showing under the iris looks calm; white showing above it looks scared.
A lifeless gaze usually needs a bigger highlight, not more detail.
In the app, pick characters with different eye styles and look at the shape of their eyelids before tracing them.
topics.practice: Draw 6 pairs of eyes in a row: 3 from the front, 3 in three-quarter view. Change only one thing each time: the eyelid, the iris or the eyebrow.

topics.title: Expressions
topics.intro: A character without an expression tells nothing. In manga, emotions read at a glance thanks to three things: the eyebrows, the eyes and the mouth. On top of them come visual codes every reader knows.

chapters.title: Eyebrows, eyes, mouth

steps.title: Eyebrows first
steps.text: They are the strongest element. Lowered toward the nose: anger or focus. Raised in the middle: sadness or worry. Very high: surprise.

steps.title: The eyes
steps.text: Wide open for surprise and fear, narrowed for laughter or suspicion, closed in an arch for a big smile.

steps.title: The mouth
steps.text: It confirms the emotion: corners up for joy, down for sadness, clenched teeth for anger, a round opening for surprise.

steps.title: All in the same direction
steps.text: An emotion is clear when all three tell the same thing. A smile with frowning eyebrows is something else: a threatening smile.

chapters.callout: Cover the lower half of the face with your hand: if the emotion still reads, your eyebrows and eyes are doing their job.

chapters.title: Six basic emotions
bullets: Joy: eyes closed in an arch or narrowed, cheeks raised, mouth wide open.
Anger: low eyebrows pulled together, creases between the eyes, teeth showing.
Sadness: eyebrows raised in the middle, eyes looking down, mouth corners down, tears at the edge of the eyes.
Surprise: very high eyebrows, small irises in big eyes, a round open mouth.
Fear: like surprise, but the mouth stretched to the sides and the body pulling back.
Embarrassment: eyes looking away, blush on the cheeks, a small wavy mouth.

chapters.title: Manga codes
bullets: A drop of sweat on the temple: unease or embarrassment.
A cross-shaped vein on the forehead: irritation, often for comedy.
Hatching on the cheeks: blushing, from shyness or love.
Blank white eyes: shock, comic rage or a character at a loss.
Vertical lines over the top of the face: despair or deep unease.
A face suddenly drawn as a chibi: an exaggerated, funny reaction in the middle of a serious scene.

chapters.title: An expression sheet
chapters.intro: Mangaka draw an expression sheet for every main character. It keeps them recognizable whatever they feel.

steps.title: The same head
steps.text: Draw the same head construction 12 times, small, from the front or in three-quarter view. The character changes emotion, not face.

steps.title: Two intensities
steps.text: For each emotion, draw two degrees: a smile and a burst of laughter, a pout and tears, annoyance and rage.

steps.title: Their personality
steps.text: A shy character doesn't laugh like an arrogant one. Keep their own habits: a crooked smile, eyebrows always slightly frowning.

steps.title: Tilt the head
steps.text: Head forward for anger, back for laughter, to the side for doubt. The emotion also goes through the angle.

chapters.callout: Keep the hairstyle and the shape of the eyes identical across the whole sheet: that is what makes the character recognizable.

tips: Make the faces yourself in a mirror or a selfie: you'll see what your eyebrows really do.
Always push a little further than you think: in a small panel, a subtle emotion goes unnoticed.
Hands help: a hand over the mouth, a clenched fist or crossed arms strengthen the expression.
For anger, the lines point toward the center of the face; for joy, they spread outward.
In the app, look at characters showing an emotion and find the eyebrows, eyes and mouth trio before tracing them.
topics.practice: Draw the same head 6 times, small, and give it the six basic emotions. Start each one with the eyebrows.

topics.title: Hands
topics.summary: A box, an arc and five fingers are enough.
topics.intro: Hands are scary, so they end up in pockets or behind backs. Yet they say almost as much as the face. Once they are reduced to a few volumes, they become much easier to build, from any angle.

chapters.title: Build a hand in four steps

steps.title: The palm as a box
steps.text: Draw a flat box, about as tall as it is wide. It tells whether we see the back of the hand, the palm or its edge. Give it some thickness right away.

steps.title: The knuckle arc
steps.text: The knuckles don't line up: draw an arc that rises to the middle finger, then drops toward the little finger. It follows the top of the palm and bends more as the hand closes.

steps.title: Fingers in segments
steps.text: Each finger is made of three cylinders that get shorter. The middle finger is about as long as the palm is tall, the index and ring fingers stop a little lower, and the little finger reaches the last joint of the ring finger.

steps.title: The thumb on its own
steps.text: The thumb doesn't start on the line of the fingers but low on the palm, near the wrist. Add the fleshy mass at its base first, then two segments. It works across from the fingers, not next to them.

chapters.callout: If your hand looks flat, the palm probably has no thickness. Go back to the box before you touch the fingers.

chapters.title: Landmarks to remember
bullets: An open hand covers roughly the face, from the chin to the forehead.
The wrist is narrower than the palm: show that change, it keeps the hand from looking like a glove.
On the palm side, fingers look shorter: the skin between them starts higher than the knuckles.
Fingers are never perfectly parallel. They spread as the hand opens and converge toward the base of the palm as it closes.
In manga, keep details to a minimum: two or three creases at the joints are enough. Slim, tapered fingers for a delicate hand, squarer knuckles for a strong one.

chapters.title: The gestures to know
chapters.intro: Four gestures cover most manga panels. Always start with the box of the palm, then bend the fingers from the knuckle arc.

steps.title: The relaxed hand
steps.text: The fingers bend slightly, a little more with each finger toward the little one. This staircase makes the hand look natural: avoid straight, parallel fingers.

steps.title: The fist
steps.text: Fold the fingers onto the palm: you only see their first segments, as blocks. The thumb closes on the outside, over the index and middle fingers, not inside.

steps.title: The pointing hand
steps.text: The index stays straight, the other fingers fold like a staircase and the thumb rests on them. Tilt the box so the gesture has a clear direction.

steps.title: The hand holding an object
steps.text: Draw the object first, then wrap the fingers around its volume. A hand is often built from what it touches.

chapters.title: The hand pointing at the reader
chapters.intro: It's the most spectacular hand in manga, and the one that impresses the most. The fingers come toward you, they overlap and the palm moves behind them.

steps.title: Start with the tip
steps.text: First draw what is closest, big: the fingertip or the fist. The rest hides behind it.

steps.title: Think in ellipses
steps.text: A finger seen head-on is no longer a long cylinder but an ellipse. Stack ellipses that shrink toward the palm.

steps.title: Overlap
steps.text: Let each shape cover the next one. These overlaps create the depth, not the details.

steps.title: Dare to exaggerate
steps.text: In manga, the near hand can be as big as the head, or bigger. The stronger the difference in size, the stronger the effect.

chapters.callout: Always check the wrist: it must stay in line with the forearm, even half hidden.

tips: Your free hand is a free model: put it in front of you, or take a photo of the gesture you need.
Draw the silhouette of the hand first, like a mitten, then separate the fingers. The gesture stays readable.
Group the fingers by two or three: four fingers well apart quickly make a stiff hand.
A thumb tucked under the fingers is the fist of someone who has never thrown a punch. Handy for a shy character.
Skip the nails and palm lines on small hands: the fewer the lines, the more confident the drawing looks.
topics.practice: Draw five box palms from different angles, add the knuckle arc and the fingers as cylinders. Finish with a relaxed hand and a fist.

topics.title: Clothes
topics.summary: See where fabric pulls, falls and folds.
topics.intro: Clothes aren't an outline placed on a character: they are fabric resting on a body, falling with gravity and folding when the body moves. Once you know why a fold exists, you no longer need to invent them at random.

chapters.title: Dress a body in four steps

steps.title: The body first
steps.text: Start with the mannequin, even a simple one. If the pose works without clothes, it will work with them.

steps.title: The points of support
steps.text: Find where the fabric really touches the body: the shoulders for a T-shirt, the waist and hips for pants or a skirt. The whole garment hangs from these points.

steps.title: The air around the body
steps.text: Between the points of support, move the outline away from the body. The looser or thicker the garment, the bigger the gap.

steps.title: The lines that go around
steps.text: Collars, sleeves, hems and belts go around the body: draw them as ellipses. They are what gives a garment its volume.

chapters.callout: A straight hem flattens the whole character. A curved one that follows the cylinder of the arm or leg brings it back to 3D.

chapters.title: Why folds appear
chapters.intro: Three forces explain almost every fold. Before you draw one, ask yourself which one is at work.

steps.title: Tension
steps.text: When a joint pulls the fabric, folds leave from that point and radiate, as at the armpits, elbows or crotch. They are long, taut lines.

steps.title: Compression
steps.text: Inside a bent elbow or behind a bent knee, the fabric bunches up. The folds are short, tight and often change direction.

steps.title: Gravity
steps.text: Where nothing holds it, fabric falls. It forms long vertical folds under a point of support, or a U-shaped curve between two points.

chapters.callout: If you can't say why a fold is there, remove it. Three well-placed folds are better than twenty.

steps.title: The pipe fold
steps.text: Parallel tubes hanging from a point of support: curtains, capes, long skirts.

steps.title: The zigzag fold
steps.text: Fabric piling up on itself: a trouser leg on a shoe, a pushed-up sleeve.

steps.title: The spiral fold
steps.text: It wraps around a cylinder: a tight sleeve, a narrow trouser leg.

steps.title: The locked fold
steps.text: In the crook of a joint bent all at once, the fabric jams into a sharp angle, like at the knee of a seated character.

steps.title: The U fold
steps.text: Fabric hanging between two points of support: a scarf, a wide collar, the sleeve of a raised arm.

chapters.title: Fabrics and manga outfits
chapters.intro: The same fold isn't drawn the same way on every fabric. That is what makes a jacket, a dress or a uniform believable.

steps.title: Thin fabric
steps.text: Silk, a light shirt: many long, thin folds that hug the body. A light, supple line.

steps.title: Thick fabric
steps.text: Coats, jackets, jeans: few folds, wide and angular. The garment keeps its own shape and stands away from the body.

steps.title: The pleated skirt
steps.text: Draw an ellipse at the waist and another at the hem, then join them with pleats that open downward. The hem makes a regular zigzag that follows the ellipse.

steps.title: The school uniform
steps.text: Sailor collar or jacket, the collar rests on the shoulders and follows their slope. Place buttons and ties on the center line of the torso: they follow its curve.

steps.title: Fabric in motion
steps.text: Capes, scarves and coat tails lag behind the body: start them from the line of action and carry the movement out to their tips.

tips: Draw each fold from its starting point and ease off the pressure: a line that thins out looks more natural.
Don't close every fold: a line that stops before the outline lets the drawing breathe.
Look for folds where the body bends. On flat areas, like a torso seen from the front, leave the fabric alone.
Bend your own arm in front of a mirror or take a photo: your T-shirt is a free reference.
An outfit tells a story: an open collar, rolled-up sleeves or a loose tie say a lot without a word.
topics.practice: Draw a standing mannequin with one arm and one leg bent. Dress it in a T-shirt and pants, mark the tension points, then draw three folds at most per area.

topics.title: Poses
topics.summary: From gesture to a living pose, readable in a second.
topics.intro: A good pose reads at a glance, even without the face or the details. The secret isn't perfect anatomy: it's a clear idea, a simple movement and a believable weight.

chapters.title: Build a pose in four steps

steps.title: The intention
steps.text: Sum up the pose in one sentence: he leaps forward, she hesitates to leave. If you can't say it simply, the drawing will stay vague.

steps.title: The line of action
steps.text: Draw a single curve, a C or an S, from the head to the foot carrying the weight. It is the movement of the whole pose.

steps.title: The big volumes
steps.text: Place the head, the rib cage and the pelvis on that curve, and tilt them against each other.

steps.title: Limbs and supports
steps.text: Add the legs first, which carry the weight, then the arms, which balance it. Details only come once the pose convinces.

chapters.callout: Thirty seconds are enough to know whether a pose works. If it fails as a sketch, details won't save it.

chapters.title: The four keys to a living pose

steps.title: Weight on one leg
steps.text: When the weight moves onto one leg, the hip rises on that side and the shoulders tilt the other way. That shift is enough to wake up a standing pose.

steps.title: Asymmetry
steps.text: Don't let both arms or both legs do the same thing. Shift the heights, change the angles: symmetry makes a character stiff.

steps.title: Balance
steps.text: Imagine a plumb line dropping from the hollow of the neck. If it lands between the feet, the character stands. If it lands outside, the character must be walking, running or falling.

steps.title: The silhouette
steps.text: Fill your pose in black. If it no longer reads, move the arms away from the body and clear the important shapes.

chapters.title: Push the pose like a mangaka
bullets: Accentuate the curve: once the pose is in place, bend the line of action a little more. What looks exaggerated in a sketch looks right in a panel.
Pick the right moment: just before or just after the blow is often stronger than the impact itself. The body is fully loaded or fully stretched.
Stretch and squash: a body launching itself gets longer, a body getting ready gathers itself in. That contrast creates energy.
Move the camera: seen from below, a character looks powerful; seen from above, vulnerable.
Bring a limb closer: a fist or a foot thrust at the reader adds depth right away.

chapters.title: Four classic poses to know how to build
chapters.intro: These poses come back in every shonen. Understand how they work once and you can vary them endlessly.

steps.title: The run
steps.text: The torso leans forward, past the feet. The arm moves with the opposite leg, and the supporting foot pushes behind the body.

steps.title: The punch
steps.text: The movement starts in the back foot, goes through the pelvis and ends in the shoulder. Turn the pelvis and shoulders toward the target, and let the other arm pull back.

steps.title: The guard
