w5d5-4.title: Your character's outfit, Your complete character
w5d5-4.text: Draw your character full body, dressed, in their signature pose: line of action, mannequin, outfit and folds, a hand gesture, and their expression.

practice.title: Build a character
practice.text: Volumes, perspective and the mannequin: the base of every body drawing. Do these sessions whenever you like, in any order.

w0d1.title: Your character in volumes
w0d1.text: The core method: a sphere, two boxes and cylinders. Learn it on a model, then do it on your own on a new character.

w0d1-1.title: Your character in volumes, Warm-up
w0d1-1.text: Fill a corner of the page with quick lines and ovals, moving from the shoulder. Just to loosen up your hand.

w0d2-2.title: The box in perspective, The method
w0d2-2.text: A box holds in 3 directions. Set them right and it turns any way you like. One face: Start with one face in perspective: a slightly distorted square. The depth: Three parallel edges leave its corners, all in the same direction. Close the box: Join the ends of the edges, and draw the hidden edges lightly.

w0d2-4.title: The box in perspective, Challenge: the stack
w0d2-4.text: Stack 4 boxes of different sizes, each one turned a different way.

w0d3.title: The jointed mannequin
w0d3.text: Volumes joined by joints: the mannequin that can take any pose.

w0d3-1.title: The jointed mannequin, The method
w0d3-1.text: The mannequin takes the character's volumes and adds joints to them. Chest and pelvis: The rib cage as an egg, the pelvis as a box, the belly joining them. The joints: Spheres at the shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees and ankles. The limbs: Cylinders between the joints, thinner towards the hands and feet.

w0d3-3.title: The jointed mannequin, Challenge: from a photo
w0d3-3.text: Find a photo of someone moving and rebuild their pose as a mannequin.

w0d4-1.title: Measuring in heads, Warm-up
w0d4-1.text: Draw 6 simple heads: a circle, then the chin. Try to keep them the same size: that's your unit of measure.

w0d4-4.title: Measuring in heads, Investigation
w0d4-4.text: Take a picture from your favorite manga and count how many heads tall the hero is. Write the number next to your drawing: every mangaka has their own rule.

w0d5-1.title: Shapes tell the character, Warm-up
w0d5-1.text: 5 circles, 5 squares, 5 triangles, fast and without a ruler.

w0d6.title: From sketch to clean drawing
w0d6.text: Wrap your volumes in a clean outline, then draw your first character of the week from start to finish.

box-1.title: How to draw a box correctly: Start with one face
box-1.text: Draw a square or a rectangle to define the front of your box. It doesn't need to be perfect.

box-2.title: How to draw a box correctly: Add depth
box-2.text: Draw edges coming out of the corners in a consistent direction. Their orientation shows how the box turns in space.

box-rotation.title: The big exercise: rotating boxes
box-rotation.text: Draw 10 to 20 boxes per session, with a different orientation each time.

mannequin-1.title: The method you'll use for all anatomy: The rib cage
mannequin-1.text: Imagine an oval volume or a box with rounded corners. Its axis shows which way the chest faces. You can simplify it to suit the manga style you're aiming for.

mannequin-2.title: The method you'll use for all anatomy: The pelvis
mannequin-2.text: Use a box that can tilt. Its front face shows the orientation of the pelvis. The hips and the legs must connect to this volume.

cylinder-1.title: The cylinder method: Draw the axis
cylinder-1.text: Start with a line that shows the direction of the arm or the leg.

cylinder-2.title: The cylinder method: Add the volume
cylinder-2.text: Place an ellipse at each end, then connect them. Vary the thickness according to the segment of the body.

cylinder-3.title: The cylinder method: Connect the joints
cylinder-3.text: Use simple shapes for the shoulders, elbows and knees. Check the orientation of each segment before drawing the final outline.

topic-basics.title: Drawing basics
topic-basics.text: Lines, circles, shapes and cubes: every artist's warm-up.

topic-eyes.title: Manga eyes
topic-eyes.text: Place them, build them, bring the gaze to life.

topic-eyes-build.title: Building an eye in four steps

topic-eyes-styles.title: One eye in every style
topic-eyes-styles.text: The same character changes completely with the style of the eyes. Knowing how to switch from one to the other means choosing who your drawing speaks to.

topic-expressions-sheet.title: An expression sheet
topic-expressions-sheet.text: Mangaka draw an expression sheet for every main character. It keeps them recognizable whatever they feel.

topic-hands.title: Hands
topic-hands.text: A box, an arc and five fingers are enough.

topic-hands-build.title: Build a hand in four steps

topic-hands-gestures.title: The gestures to know
topic-hands-gestures.text: Four gestures cover most manga panels. Always start with the box of the palm, then bend the fingers from the knuckle arc.

topic-hands-foreshortening.title: The hand pointing at the reader
topic-hands-foreshortening.text: It's the most spectacular hand in manga, and the one that impresses the most. The fingers come toward you, they overlap and the palm moves behind them.

topic-clothes.title: Clothes
topic-clothes.text: See where fabric pulls, falls and folds.

topic-clothes-body.title: Dress a body in four steps

topic-clothes-folds.title: Why folds appear
topic-clothes-folds.text: Three forces explain almost every fold. Before you draw one, ask yourself which one is at work.

topic-clothes-fabrics.title: Fabrics and manga outfits
topic-clothes-fabrics.text: The same fold isn't drawn the same way on every fabric. That is what makes a jacket, a dress or a uniform believable.

topic-poses.title: Poses
topic-poses.text: From gesture to a living pose, readable in a second.

topic-poses-build.title: Build a pose in four steps

topic-poses-keys.title: The four keys to a living pose

topic-poses-push.title: Push the pose like a mangaka

topic-poses-stock.title: Four classic poses to know how to build
topic-poses-stock.text: These poses come back in every shonen. Understand how they work once and you can vary them endlessly.

topic-hair.title: Hair
topic-hair.text: A helmet, a few locks, and movement.

topic-hair-build.title: Building a hairstyle in four steps

topic-hair-motion.title: Hair in motion
topic-hair-motion.text: Moving hair brings a panel to life, even when the character stands still.

topic-chibi.title: Chibi
topic-chibi.text: A character two to three heads tall.

topic-chibi-convert.title: Turning a character into a chibi

topic-chibi-action.title: Chibis in action
topic-chibi-action.text: With such a short body, every movement has to be exaggerated to read.

topic-perspective.title: Perspective
topic-perspective.text: Horizon, vanishing points and characters in a scene.

topic-perspective-angles.title: High and low angles
topic-perspective-angles.text: When the camera looks up or down, verticals are no longer parallel: they run to a third point. It is the angle of fights and towering heroes.

topic-light.title: Light and shadow
topic-light.text: One light source, two shadows, and volume appears.

topic-light-mood.title: Backlight and mood lighting
topic-light-mood.text: Changing the light changes the mood of a panel without touching the drawing.

topic-inking.title: Inking
topic-inking.text: Confident lines, and line weight that builds volume.

topic-inking-full.title: Inking a whole illustration
topic-inking-full.text: Inking a whole drawing takes method: the order you work in changes the result.

topic-feet.title: Feet
topic-feet.text: A wedge, a heel, and the character stands.

topic-feet-build.title: Building a foot in four steps

topic-feet-shoes.title: Shoes
topic-feet-shoes.text: A shoe is drawn like clothing: around the foot, never instead of it.

topic-page-action.title: Rhythm and action panels
topic-page-action.text: In an action scene, the layout itself becomes an effect: it speeds time up or slows it down.

topic-composition.title: Composition and framing
topic-composition.text: Where to place the subject and how to frame it.

topic-composition-study.title: Studying a pro's panel
topic-composition-study.text: Mangaka learn by taking apart other artists' work. A pro's panel is a free composition lesson.

topic-screentones.title: Black, white and screentones
topic-screentones.text: Solid blacks, screentones and black-and-white readability.

topic-screentones-moods.title: Moods: night, rain and memories
topic-screentones-moods.text: Tones aren't only for shading: they change the time and place of a scene without a word.

topic-design.title: Character design
topic-design.text: Creating a character people recognize at first glance.

topic-design-sheet.title: The model sheet
topic-design-sheet.text: A model sheet shows the character from several angles, at the same proportions. It keeps them identical from one panel to the next.

topic-action-fight.title: A fight scene in three panels
topic-action-fight.text: A good fight reads like a sentence: each panel is a word, and the reader must feel the blow before even seeing it.
